cards.title: The weather, mostly
cards.quote: It was hot. Then it wasn’t.

cards.title: Who’s related to who
cards.quote: Your aunt’s my cousin, near enough.

cards.title: Planting the rows by hand
cards.quote: Twelve hundred a day with a bar and a bucket.

cards.title: The hail that flattened the rows
cards.quote: Somebody wrote down every broken tree.

cards.title: The thing under the bridge
cards.quote: It didn’t chase me. It just looked.

cards.title: Lights past the tower
cards.quote: They went out when I stopped walking.

cards.title: Something walked the rows
cards.quote: Every row had the same track down the middle.

cards.title: We burned the fence posts
cards.quote: We kept one. We walk around it.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher, 1886 · Library of Congress

cards.title: The turtle crossing
cards.quote: We sat down in the road and waited.

cards.title: Reading by the stock tank
cards.quote: The moon on the water was enough.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher · Library of Congress

cards.title: Fog so thick the cranes walked
cards.quote: Thousands of feet in the water, nobody flying.

cards.title: When the power came
cards.quote: We stood in the yard looking at the house.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher · Library of Congress

cards.title: My great-nephew’s page
cards.quote: “Gus. Will want to leave.”

cards.title: What the foreman said
cards.quote: “Plant them like you’ll be here when they’re grown.”

cards.title: Twelve hundred a day
cards.quote: My hands still count.

cards.title: A page for every tree
cards.quote: Some pages have more in them than the tree.

cards.title: A green sky over Thedford
cards.quote: The bees came home at noon.

cards.title: The jackrabbit census
cards.quote: You can’t count them. They count you.

cards.title: The shape over Thedford
cards.quote: Ten thousand birds, asking something.

cards.title: Three days of wind
cards.quote: The sand came into the kitchen and lay down.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher · Library of Congress

cards.title: A windmill lies about the wind
cards.quote: It tells you which way. Then it lies.

art.credit: Kady B. Faulkner, Nebraska Sandhills · public domain

cards.title: The Sandhills from above
cards.quote: Somebody flew over once and said the lakes looked like dropped coins.

cards.title: The well that went sweet
cards.quote: Sixty years of pennies. Then it didn’t.

cards.title: Setting poles on the Ord line
cards.quote: You can see every pole you ever set.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher · Library of Congress

cards.title: The arch that moved
cards.quote: Nobody saw it go.

cards.title: The door in the hill
cards.quote: It’s lit inside. It isn’t for me yet.

cards.title: The clay one by the cellar
cards.quote: It looked like old paper. Then it blinked.

cards.title: The coyote that walked us home
cards.quote: At the gate it sat down.

cards.title: Not signed
cards.quote: Write it down. It won’t count.

cards.title: The seed packet with my name
cards.quote: Mine is sweet corn.

cards.title: My aunt heard it count
cards.quote: To a number that doesn’t exist.

cards.title: Aurora over Broken Bow
cards.quote: Pink first, then green like grass.

cards.title: A sod house on the Middle Loup
cards.quote: Grandmother kept a goat on the roof.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher · Library of Congress

cards.title: The landing moved forty feet
cards.quote: The river doesn’t ask. I just move the post.

cards.title: Teaching Ada to pole
cards.quote: She doesn’t fight the river. She asks it.

cards.title: Ice thick enough to drive
cards.quote: We walked it anyway, in the dark, listening.

cards.title: An owl on the pivot
cards.quote: We named the pipe, not the owl.

cards.title: Four hundred and twelve cranes
cards.quote: Then they all stood up and I lost count.

cards.title: Counting by fours
cards.quote: You count the legs and divide.

cards.title: The one that stood still
cards.quote: All night. I watched it the whole time.

cards.title: He moved the post
cards.quote: So I moved my count.

cards.title: My sister took the water
cards.quote: She waved from the middle like it was nothing.

cards.title: It looked at me
cards.quote: Long legs, like sticks that made up their mind.

cards.title: The survey that never came back
cards.quote: Every page filled. No name.

cards.title: When I’m old enough
cards.quote: I’m going too.

cards.title: Cousins in Columbus
cards.quote: Half signed, half didn’t. We still do Christmas.

cards.title: Everyone’s initials
cards.quote: Ninety squares. Some are only initials now.

cards.title: Where the two rivers argue
cards.quote: For a mile they won’t mix.

cards.title: The star hung upside down
cards.quote: On purpose. Three of us and a ladder.

cards.title: The drought year at the bluff
cards.quote: The wagon ruts came up out of the grass like they’d been waiting.

art.credit: NPS photo, Scotts Bluff · public domain

cards.title: The last wire into Omaha
cards.quote: The whole city came on, and only I saw.

cards.title: The bulb that never burns out
cards.quote: We left it on a year. It got brighter.

cards.title: Every pole you ever set
cards.quote: Look back and there they all are.

art.credit: Grain elevator, Bennet · CC0, Wikimedia Commons

cards.title: Lights in the north
cards.quote: Mother said, remember this. I have.

cards.title: The last day at the elevator
cards.quote: They swept it out and left the broom. Somebody should keep sweeping.

art.credit: Grain elevator, Kimball · CC0, Wikimedia Commons

cards.title: Her grandmother’s Survey
cards.quote: The baby is in four of the stories.

art.credit: Solomon D. Butcher · Library of Congress

cards.title: Copying the deed books
cards.quote: My hand will be in the record longer than I will.

cards.title: The lamp they keep
cards.quote: Nobody pays for it. It’s in the agreement.

cards.title: Bees in the courthouse wall
cards.quote: The deeds smell like honey in July.

cards.title: Taking the water at Brownville
cards.quote: You get in, and then you’re from somewhere else.

cards.title: Who crosses the bridge
cards.quote: I count them both ways.

cards.title: Brown water at Omaha
cards.quote: Every handful is from somewhere.

cards.title: More come back than you’d think
cards.quote: They come back carrying something.

cards.title: The lake that used to be a valley
cards.quote: My grandfather’s house is under there. On calm days you can see the chimney.

cards.title: Turning on the tower lights
cards.quote: Every dusk. Nobody sails. I turn them on anyway.

cards.title: It isn’t a warning
cards.quote: From the dam you can see the tower all the way across. It’s a hello.

cards.title: Sundays at the dam with Frank
cards.quote: He won’t sign. I won’t stop asking. We both come anyway.

cards.title: What the river keeps
cards.quote: A wedding ring, a dog’s collar, a whole canoe. I put them on the shelf by the register.

cards.title: The falls froze standing up
cards.quote: All winter, like it was holding its breath.

cards.title: Bison at the crossing
cards.quote: They came down to drink and the river went quiet.

cards.title: The canoe that came back upstream
cards.quote: Empty. Dry inside. It tied itself to my dock.

cards.title: The tracks go into the rock
cards.quote: They don’t come out the other side. I checked.

cards.title: Every cap is balanced
cards.quote: Every year one falls, and nobody hears it.

cards.title: The rhino in the clay
cards.quote: Barrel-shaped. Short legs. It looked surprised.

cards.title: A sod shelter in the badlands
cards.quote: Somebody built with the ground they stood on. The wall is mostly bones.

cards.title: Painting the shamrock
cards.quote: Every spring, in the middle of the crossroads. The trucks go around.

cards.title: A shoebox of postcards
cards.quote: Boston, Butte, Brisbane. All of them say come home.

cards.title: My mother came on a boat
cards.quote: She brought a cup of dirt from home and planted it under the porch.

cards.title: Hail the size of potatoes
cards.quote: We put them in the freezer. Proof.

cards.title: Driving the summit road
cards.quote: Three tunnels. In the middle one everybody stops talking.

cards.title: The wind took my hat to Wyoming
cards.quote: Probably. I never saw it land.

cards.title: Dry goods for the wagons
cards.quote: My great-grandfather sold needles, coffee, and a map that was mostly blank.

cards.title: The blank part of the map
cards.quote: He said the blank was where the good stories were.

cards.title: One brush at a time
cards.quote: A rib a summer. They waited twelve million years. They can wait for me.

cards.title: The calf under its mother
cards.quote: Even in the ash she was keeping it out of the weather.

cards.title: Snow that didn’t melt
cards.quote: The ash came a thousand miles and fell like snow. It never melted.

cards.title: The skull blinked
cards.quote: Once, in the afternoon. I didn’t tell the others.

cards.title: The four o’clock train
cards.quote: I race it every morning. Some mornings it lets me win.

cards.title: Cranes over the parking lot
cards.quote: Shift change. All of us stopped and looked up.

cards.title: Thirty languages on the line
cards.quote: Nobody shares one. Everybody knows the word for break.

cards.title: My sister at three in the morning
cards.quote: It’s noon where she is. She tells me her weather. I tell her mine.

cards.title: A graft from the Halsey rows
cards.quote: Ruth mailed me a twig in a wet sock. It took.

cards.title: Fires between the rows
cards.quote: Frost on the blossoms. We stayed up all night talking to the trees.

cards.title: An apple nobody has a name for
cards.quote: It tastes like the year you were born. Everyone says so.

cards.title: Every tree in one book
cards.quote: Every tree planted in the state, by hand. The book stops in 1903.

art.credit: USDA aerial index, Otoe County, 1949 · public domain

cards.title: The Sower turned around
cards.quote: Once, in a thunderstorm. He was facing west in the morning.

cards.title: Weather from three counties
cards.quote: From the top you can see it coming. I used to warn the senators.

cards.title: Checking the dome lights
cards.quote: They put the lamps on a timer. I still go up and check.

cards.title: What they say on the way up
cards.quote: Senators, schoolchildren. Everybody tells the elevator the truth.

cards.title: Sand bags to the left of me
cards.quote: It’s not half bad in the coffee, ’cause it goes right to the bottom.

cards.title: Pan-Cake, with a wet sponge
cards.quote: “Cut off my legs and call me Shorty!”

cards.title: A month late, on Mother’s Day
cards.quote: I wanted to pick violets, and to put my feet on home soil.

cards.title: The chain in the cornfield
cards.quote: He plowed up a huge chain, not far from the big cottonwood the river boats tied up to.

cards.title: The coyote on the front lawn
cards.quote: The cars line up for blocks, to study this situation.

cards.title: Into the brush
cards.quote: “Born in Rockport, married in Florence, and then moved into the brush!”

cards.title: Signed, “Sahara”
cards.quote: You can scrape sand from the bathtub with a spoon.

cards.title: Sunshine’s golden trombone
cards.quote: She lifted her golden trombone, and to me it was angelic.

cards.title: Go home, Baldy
cards.quote: “Go home, Baldy!” He always did.

cards.title: The Glad Girls leave town
cards.quote: Into the wide, wild world, with my dear parents’ blessing.

cards.title: The lights went out at the toll bridge
cards.quote: Pitch dark, and the lights went out on the Model T. No problem. I called home.

cards.title: Mother played ragtime
cards.quote: Mother played Rag-time piano like the great Joplin himself.

cards.title: First chair, and no lessons
cards.quote: “Dear Lord,” I wondered. “What is a chromatic scale?”

cards.title: Peaches from Dunning
cards.quote: She said they were spare.

cards.title: A man who knows your cousin
cards.quote: You’re Odette’s cousin’s kid. I knew it.

cards.title: They lifted all at once
cards.quote: Furious and enormous.

cards.title: The wagon ruts
cards.quote: Everybody who ever left went by here. You can see where they leaned.

cards.title: The lookout tower
cards.quote: From the top you can see three counties and nobody in them.

art.credit: Platte River State Park tower · public domain, Wikimedia Commons

cards.title: Sweeping the elevator on Sundays
cards.quote: Nobody asked. It’s just that somebody should.

cards.title: A bag pointed east
cards.quote: Somebody set it down facing the river and kept going without it.

cards.title: Every boot on the fence
cards.quote: One for everybody who walked away and kept walking.

cards.title: Kolaches after the funeral
cards.quote: Apricot, poppy seed, prune. Everybody knew whose were whose.

cards.title: Waiting out the storm
cards.quote: A stranger who keeps bees shared the culvert.

tellers.name: Ruth Ebersole
tellers.line: Every tree in these rows has a page. Sit down.

reservation.text: Only trusts people who’ve planted something

tellers.name: Priya Raman
tellers.line: The bees know the weather a day early. I write down what they say.

reservation.text: Won’t talk to someone who’s never stopped for an animal

tellers.name: Deshawn Price
tellers.line: A windmill tells you which way everything is going. Then it lies.

reservation.text: Doesn’t trust anyone who hasn’t seen the Sandhills

tellers.name: Frank Dvorak
tellers.line: I’m not signed. You can write it down. It won’t count.

reservation.text: Not signed: he only listens to something strange

tellers.name: Walt Okamoto
tellers.line: I keep a packet for every child born in the county. Ask me yours.

reservation.text: Wants to know whose child you are

tellers.name: Tomás Arriaga
tellers.line: The river moved forty feet this spring. Talk slow.

reservation.text: Won’t talk to someone in a hurry

tellers.name: Ada Nakamura-Hill
tellers.line: Four hundred and twelve. Then they all stood up and I lost count.

reservation.text: Won’t listen unless you can find something

tellers.name: Gus Pfeiffer
tellers.line: My sister took the water. When I’m old enough I’m going too.

reservation.text: Doesn’t believe grown-ups unless it’s strange

tellers.name: Marisol Ybarra
tellers.line: Every block is somebody. You just have to know who to look for.

reservation.text: Every block is somebody: name someone

tellers.name: Arne Lindqvist
tellers.line: I put light in every house from here to the river. Now I’m collecting it back.

reservation.text: Wants something that lasted since 1950

tellers.name: Odette Mbeki-Larsen
tellers.line: Everything in this room was signed by somebody’s grandmother.

reservation.text: Wants it on the record: something from 1903

tellers.name: Lou Haskins
tellers.line: Somebody has to turn them on. Nobody has to look at them.

reservation.text: Listens to people who keep doing a thing nobody asked for

tellers.name: Cal Sorensen
tellers.line: A river is just weather lying down. It keeps one thing from everybody who floats through.

reservation.text: Only listens if you’ve seen what comes down to drink

intents.label: Asks what came down to drink

tellers.name: Lan Pham
tellers.line: Something walked here before the rock was rock. I’m following it.

reservation.text: Wants proof: something from 1888 or before

tellers.name: Maeve Kinkaid
tellers.line: Half this town left. Every one of them sends a postcard in March. Whose are you?

reservation.text: Won’t say a word until you’ve talked about the weather

tellers.name: Nadia Haddad
tellers.line: The wind takes a little of the bluff every day. I drive people up before it’s gone.

reservation.text: Only trusts someone who’s taken a chance

tellers.name: Bettina Novak
tellers.line: They all died waiting for water. I brush them off one at a time.

reservation.text: Only listens to stories about animals

tellers.name: Abuk Deng
tellers.line: I run to the plant at four in the morning. The trains wait for me.

reservation.text: Trusts people who work for a living

tellers.name: Femi Adeyemi
tellers.line: Every tree here is grafted from one that was somebody’s. Ask me whose.

reservation.text: Wants to hear about weather that hurt something

tellers.name: Dot Albrecht
tellers.line: Fifty years in that elevator. I know what everybody says on the way up.

reservation.text: Wants one story to lead into the next

intents.label: Asks about the tower at night

tellers.name: Velzoe Brown
tellers.line: If you tell me you can’t play, I’ll tell you: yes you can!

reservation.text: Wants to hear about a chance you took

tellers.name: Metta Brown
tellers.line: It is the kind of day which brings reminiscing.

reservation.text: Won’t waste a thing: wants to hear what you kept

tellers.name: Imani Cole
tellers.line: I count who crosses, both ways. Tell me why you came.

reservation.text: Wants to know why you’re going

sawtooth.name: Sawtooth
sawtooth.text: Your first telling each day gets +1 Vivid.

logcabin.name: Log Cabin
logcabin.text: Retained Spare stories give +7 Weight instead of +4.

pinwheel.name: Pinwheel
pinwheel.text: Repeat copies every other event in the telling.

bearpaw.name: Bear’s Paw
bearpaw.text: Unanswered doubts cost credibility, never standing.

churndash.name: Churn Dash
churndash.text: +1 trust on the first day of every sitting.

drunkard.name: Drunkard’s Path
drunkard.text: Risk never costs standing, but gives only +3 Weight.
